extracted.intended_audience: political leaders, public-relations practitioners, educators, and organizational organizers
extracted.subtask_description: Practical guidance on planning and executing propaganda/public-relations campaigns for political leaders, civic organizations, educational institutions, and women's groups; emphasizes strategy, timing, dramatization, and institutional communications. Focuses on producing persuasive public messaging and creating circumstances that shape public opinion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use multiple methods of appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: One method of appeal is merely one method of appeal and in this age wherein a thousand movements and ideas are competing for public attention, one dare not put all one’s eggs into one basket.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not rely solely on a single medium or tactic; combine channels and techniques so messages reach different publics and cut through competing attention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Target group prejudices and loyalties
rubrics_metrics.description: Methods of propaganda can be effective only with the voter who makes up his own mind on the basis of his group prejudices and desires. Where specific allegiances and loyalties exist, ... these loyalties will operate to nullify the free will of the voter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify group identities and leaders; craft messaging that aligns with group interests and leverages existing loyalties rather than only addressing individuals abstractly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mold the public mind rather than merely please it
rubrics_metrics.description: It is not necessary for the politician to be the slave of the public’s group prejudices, if he can learn how to mold the mind of the voters in conformity with his own ideas of public welfare and public service. The important thing ... is not so much to know how to please the public, but to know how to sway the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim to shape perceptions and priorities (education/dramatization/setting agenda) rather than simply responding to polls or seeking transient popularity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meet the conditions of the public mind; create circumstances
rubrics_metrics.description: This education might be done by means of learned pamphlets ... In actual fact, it can be done only by meeting the conditions of the public mind, by creating circumstances which set up trains of thought.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design events, exhibitions, and contexts that predispose the public to receive your message (agenda-setting). Examples: staged exhibits, ceremonies, coordinated local actions that frame the issue before direct appeals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dramatize personalities and issues
rubrics_metrics.description: By dramatizing personalities, by establishing contact with the group leaders who control the opinions of their publics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use human stories, symbolic acts, and visible personalities to make abstract policy matters emotionally salient and newsworthy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish contact with group leaders and influencers
rubrics_metrics.description: Establishing contact with the group leaders who control the opinions of their publics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work through intermediaries and opinion leaders (local bosses, club leaders, organized groups) to amplify messaging and secure credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use propaganda as continuous administrative tool, not only for campaigning
rubrics_metrics.description: The expert use of propaganda is more useful and fundamental, although less striking, as an aid to democratic administration, than as an aid to vote getting. Good government can be sold to a community just as any other commodity can be sold.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain ongoing communications to explain government actions and sustain legitimacy; treat public relations as part of governance, not only electioneering.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide practical training in propaganda for political recruits
rubrics_metrics.description: I should have taken some of my brightest young men and set them to work for Broadway theatrical productions or apprenticed them as assistants to professional propagandists before recruiting them to the service of the party.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Train party operatives in staging, messaging, and professional PR techniques (practical apprenticeships, cross-sector experience) rather than assuming rhetorical talent alone suffices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manage press relationships and information flow
rubrics_metrics.description: The newspaper man looks to him for news. And by his power of giving or withholding information the politician can often effectively censor political news.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cultivate reporters as news sources, provide timely material, and understand how withholding or releasing information shapes coverage; but avoid overreliance that breeds complacency or ethical problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use media as one instrument within a strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: Although he would still use the radio, he would use it as one instrument of a well-planned strategy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine mass media messages with on-the-ground activities (exhibits, demonstrations, endorsements) so broadcasts answer an already-prepared public mood.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stage demonstrative events to dramatize abstract claims
rubrics_metrics.description: He would perhaps stage a low-tariff exhibition simultaneously in twenty cities, with exhibits illustrating the additional cost due to the tariff in force.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create physical, visible demonstrations (exhibits, boycotts, coordinated actions) that make policy consequences self-evident; involve prominent inaugurators to increase legitimacy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordinate affected groups to agitate and focus attention
rubrics_metrics.description: He would have groups, whose interests were especially affected by the high cost of living, institute an agitation for lower schedules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mobilize interest groups and stakeholders whose lived interests exemplify the issue; their activism provides authentic pressure and narrative material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-key public interest before mass addresses
rubrics_metrics.description: Then, when he spoke to his millions of listeners on the radio, he would not be ... assaulting ... the resistance of inertia; on the contrary, he would be answering the spontaneous questions and expressing the emotional demands of a public already keyed to a certain pitch of interest in the subject.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sequence communications so public addresses respond to preexisting curiosity or outrage created by prior events or framing, increasing receptiveness and reducing resistance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choose timing to maximize press receptivity
rubrics_metrics.description: Czecho-Slovakia officially became a free state on Monday... because Professor Masaryk realized that the people of the world would receive more information and would be more receptive ... on a Monday morning because the press would have more space to devote to it on Monday morning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider news cycles, calendar effects, and press capacity when scheduling announcements; small timing changes can greatly affect coverage (Masaryk example).

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid dishonest or unsocial propaganda; truth sustains persuasion
rubrics_metrics.description: The only propaganda which will ever tend to weaken itself as the world becomes more sophisticated and intelligent, is propaganda that is untrue or unsocial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Build campaigns on accurate, socially acceptable claims; dishonest messaging risks long-term erosion as publics grow more discerning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure substance: propaganda needs fertile ground and a real idea
rubrics_metrics.description: There has to be fertile ground for the leader and the idea to fall on. But the leader also has to have some vital seed to sow. ... Propaganda is of no use to the politician unless he has something to say which the public, consciously or unconsciously, wants to hear.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess public receptivity and have substantive policy or grievance that resonates; PR cannot create durable support from empty rhetoric alone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reject trial-balloon dependence; lead with informed strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: A political practice ... is the technique of the trial balloon ... It is a method which has little justification. If a politician is a real leader he will be able, by the skillful use of propaganda, to lead the people, instead of following the people by means of the clumsy instrument of trial and error.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer proactive agenda-setting based on audience knowledge to repeatedly testing policies by tentative leaks; use research and strategy to lead public opinion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Define clear objectives and know your public exactly
rubrics_metrics.description: The whole basis of successful propaganda is to have an objective and then to endeavor to arrive at it through an exact knowledge of the public and modifying circumstances to manipulate and sway that public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set measurable aims, segment audiences, research attitudes and contexts, and design interventions that alter circumstances toward the objective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Train leaders in propaganda technique as part of statesmanship
rubrics_metrics.description: The political leader of to-day should be a leader as finely versed in the technique of propaganda as in political economy and civics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include communications, staging, and public-opinion analysis in leadership curricula so leaders can responsibly direct persuasion efforts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Create institutional public-information/explanatory offices
rubrics_metrics.description: There should, I believe, be an Assistant Secretary of State who is familiar with the problem of dispensing information to the press... The United States Government should create a Secretary of Public Relations as member of the President’s Cabinet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establish trained bureaus/offices staffed by communication professionals to interpret government actions to the public and to bring public sentiment to policymakers; ensure authority to recommend disclosure and ethical standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Differentiate skilled public-relations technicians from press agents
rubrics_metrics.description: Such an official would be neither a propagandist nor a press agent, in the ordinary understanding of those terms. He would be, rather, a trained technician who would be helpful in analyzing public thought and public trends.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favor expert interpreters and analysts who synthesize public data and craft policy explanation over mere spin or image management.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use organized propaganda as a tool for social organizations (women’s groups example)
rubrics_metrics.description: Women’s most obvious influence is exerted when they are organized and armed with the weapon of propaganda. So organized and armed they have made their influence felt on city councils, state legislatures, and national congresses ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organize advocacy via coalitions and coordinated legislative programs; use displays, shops/exhibits, and targeted campaigns to turn minority ideas into law (example: rented store with tagged prices).

rubrics_metrics.name: Employ varied educational literature and programs to propagandize
rubrics_metrics.description: To propagandize these principles, the National League of Women Voters has published all types of literature, such as bulletins, calendars, election information, has held a correspondence course on government and conducted demonstration classes and citizenship schools.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use diversified content formats (bulletins, courses, demonstration classes, newsletters) to educate and mobilize members and the broader public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Professionalize organizational staff for effective advocacy
rubrics_metrics.description: Possibly the effectiveness of women’s organizations ... is due to ... the training of a professional class of executive secretaries or legislative secretaries during the suffrage campaigns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Invest in professional staff development (executive/legislative secretaries) with skills in advocacy, communications, and campaign operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leverage clubs and community organizations to address local public goods
rubrics_metrics.description: The woman’s club is generally effective on behalf of health education; in furthering appreciation of the fine arts; in sponsoring legislation that affects the welfare of women and children; in playground development and park improvement ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify community-level projects (milk in schools, baby health stations, cooking schools, loan art exhibits) where organized groups can lead and demonstrate public benefit, thereby shaping local opinion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Educators must act as propagandists for education to reach the public
rubrics_metrics.description: The normal school should provide for the training of the educator to make him realize that his is a two-fold job: education as a teacher and education as a propagandist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include public-engagement and communications training in teacher education so educators can explain educational value to broader publics and recruit support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use publicity offices and news bureaus to popularize scholarly work
rubrics_metrics.description: Many colleges have already developed intelligent propaganda ... in the form of college news bureaus. ... There is hardly a college or university in the country which does not, with the approval of the governing body and the faculty, maintain a publicity office ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain college/university publicity offices to translate research into accessible narratives, coordinate alumni and donor relations, publish newsletters, and uphold ethical standards through professional associations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance selling public value with protecting institutional mission
rubrics_metrics.description: If the university shapes its whole policy toward gaining the support of the state legislature—its educational function may suffer. ... The endowed college ... potential endowers ... often at variance with the pursuit of abstract knowledge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When crafting public-facing campaigns, protect core academic integrity; avoid becoming purely a political or donor instrument—use public persuasion to defend institutional autonomy as well as secure support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Popularize discoveries to reach wider public through skilled publicity
rubrics_metrics.description: Popularization of this message ... was due to the initiative of a young man named James Van ... It may surprise and shock some people ... the oldest and most dignified seats of learning in America now hire press agents ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hire skilled communicators to translate technical findings into narratives and media-ready stories so important scholarship gains public attention and support.
